extracted.intended_audience: Users of PARI/GP (mathematicians, numerical analysts, and programmers) doing high-precision numerical integration, summation, transforms and plotting
extracted.subtask_description: Practical reference and usage guidelines for PARI/GP numerical routines (derivative, circle integrals, Fourier/Laplace/Mellin transforms, various numerical integrators and summation algorithms, and plotting). Contains function purposes, calling conventions, parameter encodings, warnings and tuning advice for accuracy and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: derivnum(X = a, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical derivation of expr with respect to X at X = a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows numerical derivative of sin(exp(x)) at 0. Library syntax: derivnum(void *E, GEN (*eval)(void*,GEN), GEN a, long prec). Also available: derivfun(...), which allows power series for a. When a is a power series, compute derivnum(t=a,f) accordingly. Avoid the clumsier approach of defining a gp function in library mode (won't work in library mode).

rubrics_metrics.name: intcirc(X = a, R, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of (2iπ)^{-1} expr with respect to X on the circle |X − a| = R (sum of residues for meromorphic functions in the disk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tab argument is as in intnum; if computed with intnuminit endpoints should be [-1,1]. Library syntax detailed. Example: intcirc(s=1,0.5,zeta(s)) returns 1 (within tiny error). Use when computing sums of residues via contour integrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: intfouriercos(X = a, b, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of expr(X) * cos(2π z X) from a to b — the Fourier cosine transform on [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints a and b are coded as in intnum; endpoints may be infinite but oscillation encodings ([[±1], α I]) are forbidden when endpoints are infinite. Library syntax provided. Use for cosine Fourier transforms on finite or encoded intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: intfourierexp(X = a, b, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of expr(X) * exp(−2iπ z X) from a to b — the Fourier transform (note the minus sign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints coded as in intnum; infinite endpoints require no oscillation encoding. Library syntax provided. Use for complex exponential Fourier transforms; watch sign convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: intfouriersin(X = a, b, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of expr(X) * sin(2π z X) from a to b — Fourier sine transform on [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints coded as in intnum; infinite endpoints disallow oscillation encodings. Library syntax provided. Use for sine Fourier transforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: intfuncinit(X = a, b, expr, {flag = 0}, {m = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize tables for use with integral transforms (e.g., intmellininvshort), where expr is s(X) that multiplies integration weights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag ≠ 0, assumes s(−X)=s(X) (even function) which makes computation twice as fast. Useful when s(X) is expensive to compute (e.g., gamma products). Library syntax differs in argument order from GP syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: intlaplaceinv(X = sig, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of (2iπ)^{-1} expr(X) e^{X z} on the vertical line Re(X)=σ — inverse Laplace transform evaluation at z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: sig can be a real σ (assumes slow decay at imaginary infinity) or [σ, α] where α = 0 (slow), α>0 (decay like exp(−α t)). It's often beneficial to increase m by 1–2 (intnumstep) or raise σ to improve accuracy. Examples show increasing m or σ improves accuracy/time tradeoff. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmellininv(X = sig, z, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of (2iπ)^{-1} expr(X) z^{−X} on the line Re(X)=σ — inverse Mellin transform at z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: sig coded as real σ or [σ, α]; α=0 assumes exponential decrease like exp(−t), α>0 for exp(−α t) (e.g., gamma products); α usually ≈1 suffices. tab is as in intnum. Prefer intmellininvshort when possible for speed; library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmellininvshort(sig, z, tab)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fast numerical inverse Mellin transform using precomputed tab containing s(sig + i t) values (from intfuncinit format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: tab should be prepared with intfuncinit; intmellininvshort is typically much faster than intmellininv, especially when s(X) is expensive. Give a rough indication of exponential decrease in tab; omitting it can cause catastrophic loss of accuracy. Library syntax: GEN intmellininvshort(GEN sig, GEN z, GEN tab, long prec). Examples show huge speedups when tab is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnum(X = a, b, expr, {tab})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration of expr over ]a,b[; integrand may be complex- or vector-valued; assumed regular on ]a,b[ unless special codings provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints encoded as scalars or [±1] for ±∞. tab can be integer m (use 2^m sampling points) or tables from intnuminit (much faster for repeated integrals). If omitted, algorithm guesses m based on precision (intnumstep). For endpoints or singularities use [a, α] coding (α indicates local singularity exponent or decay/oscillation at infinity). Wrong singularity exponents cause catastrophic loss of decimals. Infinite endpoints have special [[±1], α] codings for slow decay (α=0), exponential decay (α>0), slow power decay (α<−1) or oscillations (α = ± k i). Choose between exponential vs oscillatory type based on relative strength; examples and important warnings provided (e.g., exp overflow, examples of improvement by truncation near singularities). Library syntax provided. Many examples illustrate tuning tab and m for accuracy and speed; use intnuminit to precompute tables for multivariate integrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: endpoint coding for intnum and related functions ([a, α] and [[±1], α])
rubrics_metrics.description: Endpoints can be specified as scalars or as two-component vectors indicating local behavior or infinity-decay/oscillation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finite, [a, α] indicates a singularity behaving like (x−a)^α (up to logs); α≥0 means regular. For infinity, [[±1], α]: α=0 (tends to zero slowly, non-exponential, non-oscillatory), α>0 (exponential decay ~exp(−α x)), α<−1 (slow power decay ~x^α; α≤−2 equivalent to α=0). Oscillatory codes: α = k*I for cos(kx)g(x), α = −k*I for sin(kx)g(x) — critical to give exact k. If oscillating part is not pure sine/cosine, expand into Fourier series and sum contributions. Choosing wrong α leads to loss of accuracy; guidance on when to prefer exponential vs oscillatory coding is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnuminit(a, b, {m = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize integration tables for intnum between a and b (a and b coded as in intnum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only compactness, singularities, speed of decrease and oscillations at infinity are considered (not function values). If m omitted, computed from current precision; otherwise integration step is 1/2^m. Reasonable m: 6–7 for 100 digits, 9 for 1000 digits. Output structure tab explained (tab[1] contains m, tab[2..] abscissas and weights). Use intnuminit to speed repeated or multivariate integrals, but intnuminit may be pessimistic — tune m by trial and error to improve speed vs accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnuminitgen(t, a, b, ph, {m = 0}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize tables for integrations from a to b using abscissas φ(t) and weights φ'(t) (user-supplied change of variables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: t ranges −∞..+∞ and φ(t) is mapped to [a,b]; flag multiplies reserved table length by 4^flag to avoid errors. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnumromb(X = a, b, expr, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical integration using Romberg-style method; suitable for smooth functions on [a,b] for low-to-moderate accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flag=0 for regular intervals; flag=1 for general driver (slow); flag=2 tailored for infinite endpoints (require ab>0 and prefer large a); flag=3 allows integrand undefined but continuous at endpoints (e.g., sin(x)/x at 0). User should not demand excessive accuracy (18–28 digits okay). No singularities should remain in interval; for improper integrals function must decrease sufficiently at infinity; avoid functions that are extremely small relative to precision on entire interval. Infinity can be approximated by a large finite number but watch underflow for rapidly decaying functions. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: intnumstep()
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the value m used in intnum and sumnum programs (integration step = 1/2^m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long intnumstep(long prec). Use to inspect or adjust default m and tune performance/accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: prod(X = a, b, expr, {x = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Product of expr for X from a to b, initialized at x (to force operation type: integer, real, or power series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialization parameter x controls computation type (exact integer arithmetic, floating point at default precision, or truncated power series with O(X^k) to bound degree and speed). Examples show huge speed savings when initializing with power series truncation for high-degree products. Library syntax: produit(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: prodeuler(X = a, b, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Product over primes between a and b (initialized at 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax provided. Use when Euler-type infinite products over primes are required; routine specialized for prime iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: prodinf(X = a, expr, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Infinite product over X starting at a; evaluation stops when relative error of expression−1 is below default precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-convergent products will loop infinitely. Expressions must evaluate to complex numbers. If flag=1, compute product of (1+expr) instead. Use prodinf1 for flag=1. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: solve(X = a, b, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a real root of expr between a and b under the condition expr(a)*expr(b) ≤ 0 (bracketed root required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Brent's method. Will error if roots are not bracketed. Can fail miserably if expr is undefined on [a,b] (e.g., solve on interval containing tan discontinuity). Library syntax: zbrent(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: sum(X = a, b, expr, {x = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite sum of expr with X from a to b, initialized at x to force computation type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initialization parameter x controls exactness/precision/type; examples show time/memory tradeoffs (summing rationals exactly vs using floating). Library syntax: somme(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumalt(X = a, expr, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical summation of an alternating series using algorithm of Cohen, Villegas and Zagier. Variable X starts at a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag=1 uses variant with different polynomials (sometimes faster). Routine is heuristic; rigorous proof requires expr values to be moments of a positive measure on [0,1]. Can sometimes sum divergent alternating series or non-exactly-alternating series; use to guess values of infinite sums. For geometrically convergent alternating series, suminf may be better. Library syntax: sumalt(...). Examples show superior accuracy for many alternating sums but also cases where suminf is faster/accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdiv(n, X, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum expr over positive divisors of n (X takes divisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrapper equivalent to enumerating divisors and evaluating expr with X lexically scoped to loop. For multiplicative functions prefer sumdivmult.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumdivmult(n, d, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum multiplicative expression expr over positive divisors d of n, assuming f multiplicative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes expr evaluates to f(d) where f is multiplicative (f(1)=1 and f(ab)=f(a)f(b) for coprime a,b). Use for number-theoretic divisor sums when multiplicativity allows optimizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: suminf(X = a, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infinite sum starting at X=a; evaluation stops when relative error of expression is below default precision for three consecutive evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expressions must evaluate to complex numbers. For slowly converging series reduce realprecision; if series is alternating or constant-sign prefer sumalt or sumpos. Examples show suminf may hang on slowly converging alternating series where sumalt succeeds. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnum(X = a, sig, expr, {tab}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical summation of expr for integer X from ceil(a) to +∞, with expr assumed holomorphic for Re(X) ≥ σ; uses intnum routines and integration on line Re(s)=σ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: sig codes σ or [σ, α] as in sumnum documentation: σ real assumes decay ≥ 1/X^2; [σ, α] with α<−1 means decay like X^α; [σ, α] with α>0 means exponential decay (α must be exact). tab must be initialized with sumnuminit. sumnum is generally faster than sumpos for slowly decreasing functions after initialization; flag≠0 assumes real-type function f(z)=overline{f(z)} which speeds up calculations. For exponentially decreasing functions prefer suminf or sumpos. Examples show pitfalls (determination problems using complex values) and tuning (increase m or specify exact α). Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnumalt(X = a, sig, expr, {tab}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical summation of (−1)^X expr(X) from ceil(a) to +∞; expr should be holomorphic for Re(X) ≥ sig.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This function uses intnum routines and is much slower than sumalt; provided for completeness only. expr must not include the (−1)^X coefficient. sig coded as in sumnum; for slowly decreasing functions indicating α is less important; for exponential decrease must indicate α exactly. tab must be initialized with sumnuminit. flag≠0 assumes real-type and speeds up computation when tab is precomputed. Prefer sumalt in practice. Library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumnuminit(sig, {m = 0}, {sgn = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize tables for numerical summation using sumnum (sgn=1) or sumnumalt (sgn=−1); sig is abscissa of integration coded as in sumnum; m as in intnuminit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precomputes tables to speed subsequent sumnum/sumnumalt calls; library syntax provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: sumpos(X = a, expr, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical summation of a series whose terms have the same sign, using Van Wijngaarden transformation to convert to alternating series then sumalt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine is heuristic and assumes expr is roughly decreasing; result wrong if expr is zero often; does not check sign of terms. For regular functions, sumnum is faster after initialization. flag=1 uses slightly different polynomials. Use sumpos to guess infinite sums of same-sign terms; sumalt or suminf may be better in other scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: plotting: high-level, low-level and PostScript functions
rubrics_metrics.description: PARI provides plotting functions (ploth* high-level, plot/rectplot low-level, ps* PostScript output) as convenience visual aids, not for heavy-duty graphics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level ploth* require little user setup. Low-level rectplot functions give primitives and manage 16 virtual rectwindows (init with plotinit; draw with plotdraw; erase with plotkill). Use plotscale for scaled windows; by default origin upper-left, y downwards. PostScript output written to psfile (default ./pari.ps) and appended on each call — remove or change psfile if needed. Plotting functions are not available in library mode (only under gp). Graphical drivers: X11, Qt, FLTK (window is forked so gp session continues). For exact printed output use printtex for TeX; ps* functions give PostScript plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: plot(X = a, b, expr, {Ymin}, {Ymax})
rubrics_metrics.description: Crude ASCII plot of expr from a to b with Y ranging Ymin..Ymax (defaults are computed from values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple ASCII plotting for quick visualization; supply Ymin/Ymax to control vertical range or let the function compute extremes.
